additionalCoursework:
The admissions recommends exploring additional courses such as anatomy and physiology, cell and molecular biology, biostatistics, Spanish, and courses that explore the cultural and social factors influencing well-being.

If you have questions regarding the prereqs or had a different path (such as in the military), feel free to reach out to the office of admissions.

medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The Cognitive Skills Program provides academic support to students in all four years of medical school. It provides services to students to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of their study and test-taking strategies. Services are tailored to student's specific needs and integrated with the curriculum.
Careers in Medicine offers support to medical students as they navigate their career paths. Led by Faculty Champions and a dedicated team of trained specialty advisors, students receive personalized guidance at every stage of their journey. 
The THRIVE Curriculum offers regular sessions covering wellbeing, career advising, and equity topics through large group, small group and peer sessions that celebrate our vibrant and diverse Robert Wood Johnson Medical School community. 
The Student Wellness Program assists students in adjusting to the stressors and pressures of medical school. Robert Wood Johnson Medical School provides free, confidential mental health services for students.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: Requests for non-medical Leave of Absence by students in good academic standing will be acted upon by the dean of student affairs. Appeals of the dean's decision may be made. Requests for a leave by students in academic difficulty will be forwarded by the dean of student affairs to the Academic Standing Committee. Requests for a medical leave of absence should be made to the dean of student affairs, and must include a letter from a health care professional. Maximum cumulative leave is 2 years.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: Our students are offered opportunities to engage in over 50 student groups and organizations.  There is an active Student Government Association. Students are encouraged to become involved in one of the many student-run organizations, which include multiple career interest groups, school chapters of AMA, SALUD, SNMA  AMSA, AMWA, AAPI, APAMSA, the umbrella organization for service opportunities "Homeless and Indigent Population Health Outreach Project", SAGA, and the International Health Interest Group, to name a few. All the leaders of these groups meet monthly with the deans to discuss issues important to the entire student body and refine their own leadership skills.  The College Advising Program is the overarching support system at the school.    https://rwjms.rutgers.edu/education/medical_education/student-life/student-groups
medSchoolStudLife.setting: In the summer of 2026, the new medical education facility within the Helix (education and translational research hub) will open across from the New Brunswick train station.   This building includes a modern mix of education spaces for learning, training, laboratory work, and discovery, including a clinical skills center with standardized patient rooms and a high-fidelity simulation. The clinical campus in New Brunswick includes the Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital and the children’s campus. The faculty practice spans sites in New Brunswick, also home to the school’s federally qualified health center and the student-run Promise Clinic.  New Brunswick is a vibrant, diverse small city at the heart of a major academic and health care corridor.  It is known for its restaurants, arts and culture, and walkable downtown core. It sits on the Northeast Corridor rail line, with direct trains to New York City and Philadelphia.
medSchoolStudLife.housing: Students generally live off-campus in the surrounding communities of Piscataway, Highland Park, and New Brunswick. Housing options range from shared private homes to townhomes and apartments.  Incoming students are assisted in finding housing with support from our medical school student onboarding coordinators.  The students host a virtual panel for accepted applicants to highlight the diversity of housing options and share what they appreciate about their chosen option.  Our onboarding coordinators also work collaboratively to share roommate-finding opportunities and landlord listings.  In-state students who live close to campus sometimes choose to commute. Graduate Student housing is available at Rutgers University.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: In addition to curricular and clinical initiatives to increase students’ comfort in conducting appropriate medical exams and providing clinical care while taking into account patient gender identity and sexual orientation, faculty and students educate their peers about issues affecting the LGBTQIA+ community.  In addition, we offer mentored research projects and seminars with faculty experts at the PROUD Gender Center of New Jersey and opportunities for students to receive advice and mentoring from faculty with relevant personal experiences.  The student organization Sex & Gender Alliance, focuses on supporting medical students and collaborates with various groups to improve health care for all. Faculty of the comprehensive Babs Siperstein Health Center at Somerset serve as student advisors and mentors to related research initiatives.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Rutgers Biomedical and Health Sciences Office of Disability Services (ODS) provides the necessary tools, resources and support for individuals with disabilities to become responsible decision-makers and self-advocates in charge of their own future. The Office of Disability Services is dedicated to the philosophy that all Rutgers University students are assured equal opportunity, access and participation in the University’s courses, programs, activities, services and facilities. We recognize that diverse abilities are a source of strength, empowerment, and enrichment for the entire university community and we are committed to the elimination of physical, instructional, and attitudinal barriers by promoting awareness and understanding throughout the university community. For more information, please see: https://oasa.rbhs.rutgers.edu/office-of-disability-services/about-ods/
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
Robert Wood Johnson Medical School has multi-faceted approach to promoting wellness in our medical students.  The student affairs office hosts the THRIVE (Together for Health, Resilience, Inclusivity, Vitality, and Equity) program across the four years.  The student government includes a student wellness officer who designs events and wellness activities.    There is a vibrant community that develops innovative approaches to wellness such as a Mind Body Medicine elective. Student groups include fun activities such as our walking/running group (Miles for Smiles), an a acapella group (Ultrasounds), and a dance group (Heart Beats). Our student affairs deans are very approachable and schedule check-in meetings with all students. 

First-year students are encouraged to complete a self-care planning document and to schedule an appointment with the Student Wellness Program. The medical school provides free and confidential mental health services for students. The Student Wellness Program assists students in adjusting to the stressors and pressures of medical school. Services include individual, couple, and family counseling, medication management, crisis intervention, and prevention-oriented groups and workshops. A diverse staff of mental health professionals who are independent of the Medical School provide these services. Participating clinicians do not evaluate students academically or play any role affecting a student's status in school.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture: Student life is vibrant at RWJMS.  Our students are actively engaged in the curriculum, spending at least three days per week on campus participating in educational activities.  Peer Mentorship begins during orientation, setting the stage for close interclass relationships and the many social opportunities to celebrate the diverse talents of the student body.  Our students engage in a breadth of opportunities on and off campus.  This includes research, student-led interest groups, multiple service opportunities in the community, and cultural celebrations.  Students support each other with study groups; they share study resources and are there to lift one another up in all the transitions of medical school.  Our students enjoy close relationships with the faculty as well.  Our students are passionate about their education and about their collective journey to becoming doctors.  What says it best is: RWJMS students are supported, engaged and happy.
medSchoolStudLife.transportationAdditionalInfo: Students will be required to travel for educational requirements throughout their four years of medical school.  Most hospitals where required clerkships take place are within 30 miles, though some are suburban without easy public transportation. Some housing options may not be within walking distance of a grocery store.
medSchoolStudLife.additionalSupportProgrameName: Cognitive Skills, Careers in Medicine, THRIVE (Togetherness for Health, Resilience, Inclusivity, Vitality and Equity), and Student Wellness Programs.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are expected to dress professionally for all clerkship experiences as well as during patient-centered experiences in pre-clerkship.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: All teaching faculty are known for their receptiveness and accessibility.  Office hours and peer tutoring are complemented by the Cognitive Skills Program (comprised of educational psychologists).
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: Students prepare for patient encounters in the first week and will have scheduled clinical experiences throughout pre-clerkship. All have longitudinal learning with underserved patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Small group case-based learning, procedure workshops, experiential learning, reflections, simulation, quality improvement activities, large group learning, teaching with standardized patients.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Core clerkships include medicine, surgery, pediatrics, family medicine, obgyn, psychiatry, neurology, emergency medicine plus critical care, PM& R, sub-internship, electives, & transition to residency
medSchoolCurriculum.prematriculationProgram: RWJMS offers students online curated materials for review of foundational science concepts and requires that all students take the corresponding quiz to establish their baseline and ensure readiness.
medSchoolCurriculum.rankStudents: We do not rank students, however performance in individual courses and clerkships is taken into consideration, among other criteria, when nominations to Alpha Omega Alpha are made.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: Generally, lectures are not mandatory with a few exceptions.  Other large group and small group non-lecture activities (e.g. team based learning, labs) are mandatory with about 3 in-person days/week..
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
2021 Launched the 5 Cs Curriculum: Curiosity, Critical Thinking, Clinical Skills, Competence, and Compassion. There are 3 phases: pre-clerkship, clerkship, and advanced clinical experiences.   School begins with a two-week Patient Centered Medicine and Health Equity course focusing on clinical skills, communication, ethics, humanism, professionalism, and critical thinking. The course continues longitudinally throughout phase 1.  Students also have longitudinal courses on evidence-based medicine and community-engaged service learning. Students complete two foundational science and anatomy courses, followed by two organ systems courses to round out their first year.   Further organ systems courses finish phase 1. Our active learning, laboratory, and doctoring course sessions require students to be on campus three days a week.  Throughout the pre-clerkship curriculum, time is given for scholarship, personal and professional development, and career advising. The curriculum includes support for success in the first licensure exam (step-1), both through regular cumulative testing as well as academic skills sessions. 

The clerkship experience begins in April of the second year and includes eight core clerkships. Every student will take one clerkship at Robert Wood Johnson University Hospital and have opportunities to take others at a variety of specialized hospitals and community medical centers. Students are provided adequate time to prepare for success in Step-2 prior to submitting their residency applications. The third phase (advanced clinical) provides opportunities for many clinical electives, critical care training, the opportunity to practice being a first-year resident, and a specialty-specific transition to residency course. Our curriculum utilizes the strengths of our faculty to ensure students are meaningfully engaged along their path to becoming physicians.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: RWJMS offers a three-year Primary Care track that provides a path for entry into a RBHS family medicine or pediatrics residency program.  This track will show learners the joy of primary care. The 3-Year program affords students the opportunity to experience enhanced continuity of care experiences and continuity of faculty mentorship.  Longitudinal relationships between faculty mentors, other health professionals, patients, and a medical student cohort are salient features of the track. Applicants offered acceptance to RWJMS have the opportunity to apply for the 3-year primary care program in the spring, and will receive a decision prior to the plan to enroll date.  We also have student interest groups, research opportunities, and mentoring for students interested in primary care.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School offers a continuum of research-oriented enrichment programs, including first-year electives and laboratory experiences, summer research training and fellowship opportunities, the Distinction in Research program, MD MS in Clinical and Translational Sciences and MD/PhD Programs, with graduate study in any Rutgers graduate program including humanities or social science. Students can pursue year-long research experiences as Student Scholars.  School research strengths include cancer, neurosciences/neurological diseases, child health, health disparities, cardiovascular,  metabolic and immunological diseases, and the molecular basis of disease.  The plethora of academic strengths of the entire Rutgers community from the humanities to biomedical engineering to population health, affords students the opportunity to realize their full potential in discovery.
medSchoolCurriculum.academicSystemText: Phase 1: the preclerkship phase occurs over 18 months with a summer break, Phase 2: The clerkship phase is 12 months in length, and Phase 3: customizable advanced experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: Service learning is curricular and student organization based. Students who have exceptional interest, leadership and commitment to service can complete a Distinction in Service to the Community.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchThesisText: All students can participate in research as well as one of our 10 Distinction programs (e.g., bioethics, climate health, community service, education, global health, leadership, research, and others)

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School has a three-phase curriculum over four years.  Students begin clinical experiences in their first year of medical school within the Patient Centered Medicine and Health Equity course.  Our ten distinction programs offer students an opportunity to highlight their passions and path in medical school with scholarly work. We are very proud of our graduates who match in competitive residency programs across the nation.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement:
School Mission: Robert Wood Johnson Medical School is dedicated to transforming health care for New Jersey and the nation through innovation and excellence in education, discovery, patient and family-centered care and addressing the health of our diverse community.

School Vision: Robert Wood Johnson Medical School will become the academic engine driving a new healthcare paradigm in New Jersey; the state's first and largest academic high-value health care system.

School Core Values: Respect, dignity, and humanism for the diverse community we serve and the diverse community we are; Wellness and resilience; Joining learners hand-in-hand with care delivery; Making patients first with safe, compassionate, high-quality care; Science to advance human health.

Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School is dedicated to excellence in medical education and to developing ethical and culturally competent physicians. Students are encouraged toward a lifelong commitment to learning and professional growth.

Education Mission:  The medical education program aspires to be a nationally recognized program.  It is a patient-centered program that prepares medical learners to become resilient and adaptable physicians who provide high value, ethical and appropriate healthcare in an ever changing system; communicate respectfully and effectively in a patient and family centered fashion; collaborate with other health care professionals to devise treatment plans and strategies for adherence and self-care, tailored to the needs and preferences of the patient; integrate the scientific underpinnings of clinical medicine and best evidence into daily practice; and who distinguish themselves as medical professionals in discovery, service and leadership.

A key aspect of our mission is having graduates who can provide care “tailored to the needs and preferences of the patient,” and therefore, we recruit and admit students whose experiences and backgrounds can enrich the learning environment and who share a wide range of perspectives. The health equity competency ensures our students understand and can serve the community in which they practice. Our students engage in a wide range of enrichment activities and distinguish themselves in areas such as research, medical education, leadership, climate health, entrepreneurship, global health, humanities, and service to the community, to name a few. They are prepared to practice in a variety of healthcare environments, from the academic medical center to local community hospitals, office practices, federally qualified health centers, and the home. They fulfill the school’s missions by pursuing a wide range of specialties, including primary care. 

Rutgers New Jersey Medical School (NJMS) and Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School (RWJMS) are moving forward with plans to integrate into a unified Future Rutgers School of Medicine, anticipated to launch in the 2027–2028 academic year, pending accreditation by the Liaison Committee on Medical Education (LCME). The earliest possible accreditation date is June 2027.
This integration will bring together the strengths of both institutions to create one medical school with two co-equal campuses in Newark and New Brunswick. The future school is designed to become a national leader in academic medicine and health equity—advancing medical education, scientific discovery, patient care, and community service to improve health outcomes for all.
To learn more about the Future Rutgers School of Medicine, please visit:
https://rutgershealth.org/future-school-of-medicine
medSchoolInformation.programAbout: The RWJMS BA/MD program is an accelerated 7-year program (3 years at Rutgers University, New Brunswick, and the full four-year medical school curriculum).  Applicants apply at the end of their sophomore undergraduate year.  The program requires a strong undergraduate GPA, a strong MCAT, and experiences that demonstrate applicants' passion for medicine and community engagement. As students utilize their first year of medical school coursework to fulfill their undergraduate degree, they are advised to work with their undergraduate advisor to ensure success.  The medical experience provides a full opportunity to pursue their passion.

medSchoolApplication.cbcRequired: Yes, both the certiphi and a state specific background check are required.
medSchoolApplication.applicantResponseToOffer: We request a non-binding response in two weeks.  Please call the admissions office if you need to discuss as we are happy to work with applicants.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText: We understand that applicants who have been out of school for some time may find it challenging to obtain recent academic letters and are open to receiving alternative relevant letters. If you have graduated for three or more years at the time of application, please ensure that your letters come from recent contacts.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance: RWJMS requires three letters of recommendation (or a composite committee evaluation) and permits up to 7 letters. The three required letters should be academic or professional in nature. We encourage applicants to select a variety of letter writers.  We ask that your letters come from individuals who know you well, such as faculty members, employers, or volunteer managers. Letters should offer the admissions committee insight into the applicant's professional and personal qualities. We encourage you to seek guidance from your health professions advisor, whether or not they offer a committee letter.
medSchoolApplication.typicalInterviewDay:
The Interview Day consists of: 
1.  Comprehensive introduction to the MMI format and specifics about the admissions process from the admissions officers; Applicants get a first-hand experience of the supportive nature of education staff.
2. Prior to the interview day, our Student Ambassadors offer an information session that includes topics on the curriculum, school culture, organizations, enrichment opportunities, and student life, followed by a Q&A.  The student ambassadors share their insights with the applicants.
3. A 45-minutes Q&A with an education dean giving an up close and personal view of the accessibility and responsiveness of faculty, their perspectives about the learning environment of the school, advice on how to succeed in medical school and how faculty support students in achieving their professional goals 
4. A seven-station MMI conducted by both faculty and students, lasting approximately one hour and ten minutes.
medSchoolApplication.interviewInvitations: Interview invitations are sent monthly from August through March.
medSchoolApplication.interviewFormat: RWJMS will use an MMI format for applicants in 2027.  Those applying to MD/PHD,  BA/MD, and approved early assurance will additionally participate in 1-on-1 interviews. In the 2028 cycle, all applicants will complete both interview formats.
medSchoolApplication.regionalInterview: RWJMS has not established a regional interview option.
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: RWJMS is determining whether in-person interview options will be used.  For applicants who are abroad or might have hardship, virtual will always be available.
medSchoolApplication.secApplSentTo: Secondary applications are sent to all applicants upon receipt of your verified primary AMCAS application.
medSchoolApplication.secApplEarliestDtText: Our secondary application is sent and submitted through the admissions portal.
medSchoolApplication.secApplLatestDtText: Though our deadline to submit the secondary application is January 15, 2027, we strongly encourage applicants to submit early (prior to October 2026).
medSchoolApplication.edpAvailableTxt: Early-decision applicants undergo the same review process as regular MD applicants.  Interviews begin in August.  Please be mindful of the EDP timeline and how it can shape the rest of your cycle.
medSchoolApplication.ctsRequired: No required relationship.  International applicants will only be reviewed if they have taken college/university coursework in the US or Canada.
medSchoolApplication.stateResAfterMatric: Possible one year after matriculation.  Matriculated students should work with the registrar office to apply for a change in residency status.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: RWJMS aims to increase the number of out of state students who matriculate, however NJ residents will always be the majority of matriculating students.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The supportive learning environment at RWJMS starts with the dedicated and approachable staff in the Office of Admissions. We encourage applicants to explore the RWJMS admissions website, where they can find answers to many frequently asked questions. Additionally, applicants have the opportunity to register for a virtual admissions open house.

An application is considered complete when the Office of Admissions has received the AMCAS application, MCAT scores, a pre-professional advisory committee letter or three individual letters of recommendation, the completed secondary application (including the CASPer™ result or AAMC PREview exam result), and the application fee or fee waiver. Applicants are required to have completed a minimum of three years of college (90 semester hours of coursework, excluding military and physical education) and to provide MCAT scores from a test taken within three years prior to the application and no later than September of the application year. We strongly encourage early submission and completion of the application. Applicants may register and take the CASPer or AAMC PREview exam at any point before or after submitting their AMCAS application.

RWJMS is committed to building a well-rounded class. We believe that students with a variety of interests and experiences enrich the educational environment for all learners. With an increasing focus on active learning and self-directed education, the opportunity to explore critical issues such as health and disease, the physician-patient relationship, and the impact of culture on patient care is significantly influenced by the student body. Given the high number of qualified applicants, those selected for interviews are chosen based on their potential to contribute something unique to RWJMS. While applicants will not have identical profiles, they will each demonstrate the potential to bring valuable perspectives to both the RWJMS community and the medical profession. The admissions committee utilizes a mission-focused review.  Selection for interviews is based on a comprehensive evaluation of the applicant's experiences, achievements, personal qualities, and potential to enhance the learning environment and further our mission. All components of the application, including academic records, personal and professional experiences, letters of recommendation, personal statement and secondary responses, and CASPer™ or AAMC PREview assessments, are considered in the review process.  Final admission decisions are made by the admissions committee after the interview results are reviewed.


Response to COVID-19 - Information for the 2027 Admissions Cycle
Pass/Fail Coursework: RWJMS will accept pass/fail grades for prerequisite and science coursework taken during the spring, summer, and fall 2020 semesters, as well as the spring of 2021. Ideally, applicants will have science course grades for the majority of their courses, but we will always evaluate the application as a whole.
Online Coursework and Labs: Due to the transition to online courses during the pandemic, RWJMS will accept online courses from applicants who were enrolled during this time. However, we prefer applicants to have primarily in-person coursework, including some in-person labs or hands-on research experience.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: Our committee will consider all scores. Reviewers most value the latest scores.  When considering MCAT scores, reviewers look at timing, the applicant's circumstances, and the change across scores if applicable. Our reviewers do believe the MCAT, in combination with other application components, provides valuable insight and is a consideration when assessing an applicant's readiness for the rigors of medical school.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScreenAdditionalInfo: RWJMS encourages applicants to have an MCAT score above 504 with all subsections above 123, but has no minimum requirement for screening.  Our median MCAT score last cycle was 514, with subsection scores of 127-128.  The committee does accept a breadth of scores and knows that the best prediction of success in medical school is a combination of GPA, MCAT, and personal characteristics/experiences.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: RWJMS encourages applicants to demonstrate strong academic performance.  We have no minimum gpa requirement for screening. Our median cumulative undergraduate gpa of matriculated students was 3.8 last cycle.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: Applicants pursuing a postbac/graduate program in science are expected to demonstrate mastery in the coursework. We encourage applicants to complete, or have completed, a year of their master's program before submitting their application.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: For students in a postbac program or a masters in science/biomedical science program, we do require having 15 credit hours showing on the AMCAS application.  For applicants who have pursued or are pursing a non science masters such as an MBA, we have no minimum requirements.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: We accept community college coursework; however, we recommend that upper-level science coursework, such as biochemistry, be completed at a four-year university/college. We do accept candidates who have completed an associate's degree and transferred to complete their bachelor's degree.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Please note that we will not consider any letter of intent or interest in the application review.  We welcome limited notices of updates or achievements.  A general guideline is that those should be limited to two per cycle.  Update letters should be uploaded to the application portal, and a notice of the upload should be emailed to the admissions office.  Interviewed applicants placed in the high-priority category are permitted to submit a further update or letter of interest in March/April of the cycle.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Our goal at Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School is to recruit and train medical students who will become the future healthcare leaders of New Jersey, the nation, and the world.  We are committed to the following We C.A.R.E. (contextualize, affirm, represent, empathize) principles. Graduates of our M.D. program are physicians prepared for entry into the practice of medicine within a postgraduate training program. They possess the knowledge and skills to function in a broad variety of clinical situations and to render a wide spectrum of patient care.  Our technical standards represent guidelines of the nonacademic skills necessary to provide safe and effective patient care as a medical student in our program.   Please see the link for our technical standards regarding: Observation, Communication, Motor, Intellectual-Conceptual, Integrative and Quantitative Abilities, Behavioral and Social Attributes, and Professionalism

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid:
The school grants scholarships to incoming and continuing students based upon academic merit and financial need.  All financial aid awards consist of a package of loans and grants (based on merit and need) when funds are available.  Financial counseling services are available pre-matriculation and financial wellness programming occurs throughout the four years.  Graduating students can apply for the Rising Stars Program which offers $200,000 to select students who choose to complete their graduate medical education and match at a Rutgers or RWJBarnabas Health accredited residency and
remain employed by Rutgers or RWJBarnabas Health following completion of their graduate medical education program(s).  

Additionally, our graduates may apply for The Primary Care Practitioner Loan Redemption Program which promotes access to primary care services in medically underserved areas of the State of New Jersey by improving the distribution of primary care health providers.
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition and fees are payable in advance each semester. Tuition increases are anticipated to be less than 2%.  A student may arrange with the Cashier's Office to follow a deferred payment plan. No degree will be awarded to any student until all financial obligations to the school have been satisfied. Students who withdraw from medical school of their own accord prior to completion of one third of the unit of time following the date of registration may be granted an 80% tuition refund at the discretion of the Dean or the designee.  Students who are taking a reduced course load through a flexible curriculum option but who do not repeat any course at Robert Wood Johnson Medical School will have their tuition divided among the years that they are attending but will pay no more than the equivalent of four years of full tuition during their enrollment at Robert Wood Johnson Medical School. medSchoolPrograms.info:
The post-baccalaureate program is a one-year graduate program run by the Rutgers School of Graduate Studies in conjunction with RWJMS teaching faculty. The Office of Admissions offers baccalaureate/masters students who successfully meet academic criteria and are recommended by their program director an opportunity for an interview.

There are summer enrichment programs for undergraduate students, which provide academic support and career development through mentoring and clinical activities.

The school offers a self-directed online summer pre-matriculation program via a faculty-designed course.   This program is comprised of a series of podcasts and virtual modules reviewing foundational science material and includes readiness tests to inform incoming students and faculty of any foundational science learning gaps that can be supported by the school's office of academic counseling.

medSchoolPrograms.name: MD/MSTCS
medSchoolPrograms.programLength: This program requires a scholar year to complete resulting in 5 years for the dual degree.
medSchoolPrograms.deadline: Apply while in medical school after consultation with the student affairs dean.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
MD/PhD:  RWJMS, Rutgers School of Graduate Studies, and Princeton University offer a joint MD/PhD program with fellowships and tuition support. Students apply to the MD/PhD program directly in conjunction with their application to RWJMS.

RWJMS has the first in the country,  PharmD/MD with the Ernest Mario School of Pharmacy of Rutgers University. Students apply to RWJMS while in the graduate portion of the PharmD program. Other Rutgers MD/Grad degrees include MD/MPH; MD/MBA; MD/MS Clinical and Translational Science. Students apply to these programs after MD acceptance or at any point following matriculation. There is a wide array of programs across disciplines at the university. Some students opt to obtain an additional graduate degree at an institution outside of Rutgers by pursuing the “student scholar” option.  Please also explore our distinction programs: https://rwjms.rutgers.edu/education/medical_education/distinction-programs

medSchoolPrograms.name: PharmD/MD dual degree with the Ernest Mario School of Pharmacy of Rutgers University

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: The AAMC asks accepted students to narrow their offers to three schools by April 15. Accepted students are also asked to narrow the number of acceptances held to three by April 15th. They may continue to hold alternate lists.

It is helpful to our admissions process and informative for alternate list applicants to have all accepted students select "plan to enroll" by May 1.  We request that you narrow your schools held to one and select 'plan to enroll' by this date.  Please contact admissions with questions. You may remain on all alternate lists. Applicants are required to select Plan to Enroll by May 1, 2026

MD/PhD accepted applicants are requested to select commit to enroll by May 18, 2026. The first research rotation for MD/PhD students is set for June 1, 2026.  Please reach out to the MD/PhD director if you have any questions or concerns.

At 21 days before orientation, accepted students matriculating to RWJMS are asked to withdraw from all other options for medical school and select Commit to Enroll.  Please call the office with questions/exceptions and we will work with you. Applicants are required to select Commit to Enroll by June 29, 2026.

 If both are submitted, we will utilize the higher score. https://takealtus.com/welcome_to_takealtus/

One Situational Judgement Test (SJT) is Required - You must submit a minimum of one SJT score for your application to be considered complete; a PREview® score will satisfy this requirement.  Applicants may submit either PREview or CASPer. 
 If both are submitted, we will utilize the higher score. https://students-residents.aamc.org/aamc-preview/aamc-preview-professional-readiness-exam

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: Robert Wood Johnson Medical School offers a three-year accelerated primary care track program. This track includes early clinical experiences in family medicine or pediatrics, as well as a summer course during the pre-clerkship phase of the curriculum.  Students complete all MD program requirements by the end of the third year. After successfully completing the curriculum, students are eligible to match into one of our affiliated family medicine or pediatrics residency programs.
medSchoolMdPathway.spotAvailable: The three-year accelerated primary care program has availability for three students committed to pediatrics and four students committed to family medicine.  The aligned residency programs include RWJMS Pediatrics residency, RWJMS Family Medicine New Brunswick, RWJUH Somerset Family Medicine, and CentraState Family Medicine Residency Freehold.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants: Applicants accepted to Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School with a demonstrated interest in pursuing primary care are eligible to apply to the three-year track.  Currently, there are only two specialities available in the program. Students who are in the MD/PhD program or plan to pursue a dual degree are ineligible.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationDeadline: We open the application to accepted students in early March, and the deadline to apply is March 26, 2027.
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Accepted RWJMS applicants notify the office of admissions of their desire to apply in late March.  Their short essays from their secondary and their full AMCAS applications are sent to a subcommittee for review.  Those identified to continue with the application interview with two faculty and one resident in the specialty they are applying to, as well as the program director.  Decisions after the interview are released before the April 30th CTE date.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq: Applicants should be confident that they can graduate in three years, be self-directed learners, pass all requirements within the time frame, and have a commitment to family medicine or pediatrics.  There are no opportunities for advanced clinical electives in the three-year track. The school can open applications to current M1 students when space is available and will support students who wish to transition to the four-year program.
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option for all Three-Year MD students

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistInformation: We typically have a high priority and waitlist group.  In most cycles we do offer spots to applicants on the alternate list.
medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: We accept updates and letters of interest from high priority applicants.  Offers from the alternate list will not be made prior to May 1st and can continue through July..

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
In the spirit of preparing undergraduates for the rigors of medical school, of supporting development in the humanities and psychosocial realms, and of understanding the constraints some students may have in meeting all course requirements, Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School has adopted a flexible approach to prerequisites:
One year of biology, one year of general chemistry and one year of physics, all with laboratories.  One semester of organic chemistry with lab and one semester of biochemistry. One semester of mathematics is required which can be statistics/biostatistics.   Two semesters of writing-intensive coursework (such as English or bioethics or history) are required.  Recommended courses include physiology, psychology, sociology, public health, biostatistics, humanities, and Spanish.  AP, community college, and online course credits will be considered for some courses on a case-by-case basis. We allow applicants to send questions and inquire about alternatives.
medSchoolSelection.oldestPrereqDate: We do not have a cut-off date, but we generally recommend no older than 8 years.
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: Admission is determined based on pre-professional evaluations, pre-professional attributes, relevant experiences, demonstrated competencies, academic performance, MCAT scores, and performance during the interview. While Rutgers Robert Wood Johnson Medical School is a state institution of New Jersey, we are committed to increasing the acceptance rate of out-of-state (OOS) applicants and encourage individuals from outside New Jersey to apply. We believe a well-rounded student body enriches the educational experience for all students. Our selection and recruitment process involves a comprehensive review of each applicant’s experiences, personal qualities, and their potential to contribute to and enhance the learning environment. Interviews are conducted by invitation only.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: It is required that you demonstrate awareness of the profession and be comfortable talking to people who are seeking medical care.  There are many experiences that provide opportunities to gain an understanding of the role of a physician and test one's comfort in the clinical environment.  Though shadowing and volunteering are typical, those can be replaced with alternate experiences. We ask that you be thoughtful in how you describe your exploration of the profession. There are many experiences that may demonstrate awareness, including paid work experiences,  providing phone companionship to a senior, caring for a grandparent, clinical research, and many others.
